summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes and a history of Charcot arthropathy was admitted for worsening right foot pain and a low-grade fever. Imaging showed no fracture, but she was diagnosed with a flare of right Charcot arthropathy. She had leukocytosis and a positive urinalysis, leading to a diagnosis of asymptomatic urinary tract infection caused by E. coli, treated with ciprofloxacin. Her elevated creatinine was attributed to dehydration and recent antibiotic use, with improvement by discharge. She was found to have anemia and B12 deficiency but declined supplementation during admission. She was discharged with a CAM walker, instructions for non-weight bearing, and follow-up plans with podiatry and her primary care provider.
problems: Urinary tract infection, site not specified
